# JMA Unified Hypocenter Catalogue (the Seismological Bulletin of Japan)

`jma_hypocenter` · adapter 1.0.0 · makes `seismic_catalog` tokens

|---|---|

## Terms

JMA's Terms of Use are compatible with Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; the data may be used under CC BY 4.0 with the source credited.

## Cite

- Japan Meteorological Agency, The Seismological Bulletin of Japan, hypocenter files. https://www.data.jma.go.jp/eqev/data/bulletin/hypo_e.html

## Access

One zip per year under `https://www.data.jma.go.jp/eqev/data/bulletin/data/hypo/` (1997 in two parts), each one fixed-width text file. Downloaded once each, at most one request per second, cached by hash.

## From the source to the token

| Token slot | Comes from |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `event` |
| `lat, lon` | columns 22-28 and 33-40, degrees + minutes (JGD2000/2011 ≈ WGS84) |
| `depth_km` | columns 45-49 (F5.2, or 1 km depth slices) |
| `time` | columns 2-17, Japan Standard Time, minus 9 hours to UTC |
| `value` | magnitude 1, columns 53-54 (letters for negative values) |
| `qualifiers` | magnitude_type ← column 55 (J/D/d/V/v → Mj, W → Mw, B → mb, S → Ms) |
| `provenance.record` | `jma:<date time>:<lat>:<lon>;type=<letter>;flag=<col 96>` |

## Uncertainty

The record has origin-time and location errors, kept out of the token for now; magnitude 1σ is an assumed 0.2 (`uncertainty_basis: assumed`).

## Known issues

- From April 2016 an automatic process roughly doubled the number of small earthquakes located; completeness drops at that date.
- Offshore completeness is far worse than on land; a region states one magnitude it trusts.
- Records located by USGS or other agencies (types U, I) are left out.
